q: How is NADP reduced in the light-dependent reactions?
options: Excited electrons from P700 pass via ferredoxin to NADP reductase, which forms NADPH using H+
Electrons released by photolysis pass straight to NADP+ dissolved inside the thylakoid lumen
NADP+ is reduced by ATP synthase each time a group of protons flows through it into the stroma
NADP+ is reduced by accepting electrons from O2 molecules at the very end of the transport chain
explanation: PSI absorbs light (P700) and emits high-energy electrons to ferredoxin, an iron–sulfur protein on the stromal side. The enzyme NADP reductase transfers 2 electrons plus H+ to NADP+, forming reduced NADP. P700+ is refilled by electrons arriving from PSII via plastocyanin. Using up H+ from the stroma also steepens the proton gradient.
